out-of-project file links show an error and leave app usable.\\r\\n- Tests cover path normalization, internal editor routing, VS Code fallback, and error handling.\\r\\n\\n===== F_90_redesign_add_new_card_dialog.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_90\\r\\ninternalId: eb3a4820-0edb-4161-8fe5-926a981d2c8f\\r\\ntitle: redesign add new card dialog\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: d97a054f-5a67-47bb-9070-df874cf9148e\\r\\n---\\r\\nReference mockup: `New Card Dialog.dc.html` (desktop + mobile side by side, light/dark toggle top-right).\\r\\nStyle tokens and component conventions: `STYLE_GUIDE.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Why\\r\\n\\r\\nThe current dialog is low-value and hard to scan:\\r\\n\\r\\n* The markdown template (Goal / Current status / Details / Tasks) is pre-inserted and rendered as large bold headings, so it dominates the dialog, doesn't look editable, and must be deleted for most cards.\\r\\n* Title â€” the one field that always matters â€” is visually secondary.\\r\\n* Type is a dropdown, which costs two clicks for a short, known list.\\r\\n* The footer's \\\"Adds to \\\\\\\" is static text, so the target column can't be changed without closing the dialog.\\r\\n* Net result: lots of empty space, little usefulness.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Scope\\r\\n\\r\\nTwo presentations of the same form and the same state:\\r\\n\\r\\n* **Desktop** â€” centered modal dialog over a scrim.\\r\\n* **Mobile** â€” full-height sheet.\\r\\n\\r\\nSame fields, same validation, same submit behavior. Only layout, control sizing, and chrome differ. Breakpoint should follow whatever the app already uses; do not introduce a new one.\\r\\n\\r\\n***\\r\\n\\r\\n## Field order and behavior (both platforms)\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1. Title â€” primary field\\r\\n\\r\\n* First element in the body, autofocused on open.\\r\\n* Visually the largest input: \\\\~17px/600 on desktop, \\\\~18px/600 on mobile.\\r\\n* Placeholder `Card titleâ€¦`.\\r\\n* Required. Create is disabled (or shows an inline error) while empty. Trim before submit.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2. Type â€” single-select pill row\\r\\n\\r\\n* Replaces the dropdown with one-click pills.\\r\\n* **Types are dynamic.** Render one pill per type from the app's existing type source (same source the board/card already uses). Do not hard-code type names, count, or order â€” the row must work for 2 types or 12.\\r\\n* **Colors are dynamic.** Each pill shows a small round dot (8px) filled with that type's own color, taken from the type record. Never hard-code hex values per type; if a type has no color, fall back to a neutral token (`--text-4`).\\r\\n* Selected state: tinted background + border in the app's primary token, primary text color. Unselected: subtle track background, secondary text, transparent border; hover raises contrast.\\r\\n* Default selection: the app's existing default type (first in the list if there is no configured default).\\r\\n* Overflow: desktop wraps to multiple lines; mobile scrolls horizontally in one row (no wrap, no visible scrollbar chrome).\\r\\n* Keyboard: arrow keys move between pills, Space/Enter selects; the row is a single tab stop (radiogroup semantics â€” `role=\\\"radiogroup\\\"` with `role=\\\"radio\\\"` + `aria-checked` children).\\r\\n\\r\\n\\n===== F_91_remove_finished_reasoning_blocks.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_91\\r\\ninternalId: 3ffa4da3-1e0f-4930-ad38-6bf247b13c52\\r\\ntitle: remove finished reasoning blocks\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: eb3a4820-0edb-4161-8fe5-926a981d2c8f\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nwhen a reasoning output of an agent finishes, we should remove the block\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current state\\r\\n\\r\\nCodex reasoning is stored as an `AgentConversationEvent`. Streaming updates replace the same event by `providerItemId`, changing its status from `inProgress` to `completed`. `ActionConversationChat` currently renders every reasoning event, so completed reasoning blocks remain visible during the live run and in reopened conversations. Failed and declined reasoning already use the error presentation.\\r\\n\\r\\n## implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Filter conversation feed activities in `ActionConversationChat`: omit only events where `type === 'reasoning'` and `status === 'completed'`.\\r\\n- Keep in-progress, failed, declined and unknown-status reasoning visible.\\r\\n- Keep completed reasoning events in conversation data and persisted history; this is a presentation-only change.\\r\\n- Update chat tests for live completion, reopened conversations, failed/declined reasoning and unaffected non-reasoning activities.\\r\\n\\r\\n## acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- In-progress reasoning is visible.\\r\\n- A reasoning block disappears when its status becomes `completed`, including after reopening a conversation.\\r\\n- Failed and declined reasoning remains visible with its error state and content.\\r\\n- Completed non-reasoning activities remain visible.\\r\\n\\n===== F_94_no_prefill_prompt_running_conv.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_94\\r\\ninternalId: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\\r\\ntitle: no prefill prompt running conv\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 3ffa4da3-1e0f-4930-ad38-6bf247b13c52\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen an agent is waiting for a response, but the action popup was closed or on the wrong 'action', then when the user clicks on the action to view the conversation and answer, the input box is prefilled again with the action's prompt. this is annoying cause it needs to be removed.\\r\\n\\r\\nso, when activating an action that has a running conversation, don't prefill the input\\r\\n\\r\\n# Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`useActionPopupController` prepares an action's stored prompt for a new conversation. When popup opens on another action, or reopens while execution state is being restored, that prepared prompt can remain in `promptState` when user selects action with a `queued`, `running`, or `waitingForInput` conversation.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Give active execution its own prompt identity, including before active-child metadata arrives.\\r\\n- When active action is selected, seed editor only from its shared user-entered draft; otherwise show empty input.\\r\\n- Invalidate pending prompt preparation and bump `promptResetToken` when action becomes active.\\r\\n- Keep stored-prompt prefill for idle actions starting new conversations. Keep command actions unchanged.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Selecting or reopening action with active conversation does not prefill its stored action prompt.\\r\\n- Existing user-entered draft for active conversation is restored.\\r\\n- Late prompt-preparation result cannot overwrite active conversation input.\\r\\n- Idle agent actions still prefill stored prompt.\\r\\n- Controller and popup tests cover action switching, popup reopen, draft restore, and preparation race.\\r\\n\\n===== F_95_integrate_into_project_should_track_commit.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_95\\r\\ninternalId: e5b95f2c-cd0c-4623-8e12-d0c497447e71\\r\\ntitle: integrate into project should track commit\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\n - design/activity/card__e5b95f2c-cd0c-4623-8e12-d0c497447e71.json#conversation=agent-4e6f97b9-647e-49fc-93f7-cf09e5eff1aa\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 9ef42f8e-d6f7-4514-8e4a-5555318c4b51\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`WorktreeSelector` integrates an assigned card through `WorktreeService` and the Electron worktree service. The backend checkpoints primary-worktree changes, rebases the card branch when behind, then fast-forwards the project branch. The operation returns no commit metadata.\\r\\n\\r\\nCard commit history reads tracked `/activity/card__.json` files. Only action executions add commit references, so commits integrated from the selector are absent unless an action already recorded them.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Add a card-specific integration request containing `cardInternalId` and `projectFolder`; project-level worktree integration remains untracked.\\r\\n- After any rebase, squash the card branch's complete change onto the project branch and create one integration commit. Do not fast-forward or retain the card branch's individual commits on the project branch.\\r\\n- Resolve the integration commit's activity metadata, then append one system activity record containing only that commit and labeled `Integrate into project` to the card's primary-checkout activity file. Do not model it as a user action.\\r\\n- Commit the activity-file update through the existing serialized activity writer. Return only after both integration and history persistence finish, so existing card-history reload and diff UI show the integration commit.\\r\\n- If applying or committing the squash fails, restore the primary checkout to its state after the primary-worktree checkpoint and before the squash attempt.\\r\\n- Failed integration writes no activity record. If integration succeeds but activity persistence fails, report that partial failure clearly; never claim tracking succeeded.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Integrating a card worktree with one or several outgoing commits creates and records exactly one squash commit under the card's stable `internalId`.\\r\\n- The squash commit contains the combined change between the project branch and the rebased card branch. Primary checkpoint and activity-file commits are not included.\\r\\n- The squash commit appears once under `Integrate into project` in the existing card commit selector and opens one combined diff for the integration.\\r\\n- Integration with no outgoing commits or no combined change remains rejected and creates no activity record.\\r\\n- Failed integration creates no activity record. History-persistence failure after a successful squash commit is visible.\\r\\n- Project-level worktree integration creates no card activity.\\r\\n- Tests cover one and several source commits producing one squash commit, rebase before integration, stable card ownership, squash cleanup and persistence failure paths, and project-level exclusion.\\r\\n\\n===== F_96_ctrl_enter_on_action_input.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_96\\r\\ninternalId: d33002d3-ee0e-4c08-8e26-36f790500ee2\\r\\ntitle: ctrl enter on action input\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nwhen pressing ctrl + enter on action input, the input is sent, this is good, but before this happens, the input box still adds an enter, which should not be the case.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`ActionAgentPrompt` handles `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` on the prompt wrapper during event bubbling. MDXEditor handles `Enter` first, inserts a newline, then the wrapper flushes and sends the changed prompt.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Intercept `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` during capture, before MDXEditor handles the key.\\r\\n- Prevent default behavior and stop propagation, then flush the latest prompt before running the existing shortcut callback.\\r\\n- Keep plain `Enter`, `Shift+Enter`, and disabled shortcut behavior unchanged.\\r\\n- Extend `action_agent_prompt.test.tsx` with regression coverage proving the editor does not receive the send shortcut.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- `Ctrl+Enter` sends current prompt without inserting a newline.\\r\\n- `Meta+Enter` has same behavior.\\r\\n- Prompt is flushed before send callback runs.\\r\\n- Plain `Enter` and `Shift+Enter` still insert newlines.\\r\\n\\n===== F_98_worktree_vs_project_folder_placeholders.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_98\\r\\ninternalId: ff356504-eed4-47f3-bb38-2c749b6fcba6\\r\\ntitle: worktree vs project folder placeholders\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: d33002d3-ee0e-4c08-8e26-36f790500ee2\\r\\n---\\r\\nWe have 'rootProjectFolder' placeholder. this currently maps to the folder that the agent is running on, so it could the the main project folder or a worktree. \\r\\n\\r\\nWe need to improve this and split it up in `worktree-folder` and 'project-folder' where the last one always references the main project folder while 'worktree-folder' references the folder that the agent is currently running in.\\r\\n\\r\\nAlso, we need to add the 'releases-folder' as well\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n- `{{rootProjectFolder}}` exists in action prompt/command and diff-command placeholder sets.\\r\\n- Action execution resolves it to the execution checkout, which may be the opened project folder or a linked worktree. Diff commands resolve it to the opened project folder.\\r\\n- Action editor insertion controls and user documentation expose only the existing placeholder.\\r\\n\\r\\n## implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Replace `{{rootProjectFolder}}` everywhere with `{{worktree-folder}}` and `{{project-folder}}`; do not keep a legacy alias.\\r\\n- `{{worktree-folder}}` resolves to the absolute execution checkout path. When no linked worktree is selected, it equals `{{project-folder}}`.\\r\\n- `{{project-folder}}` always resolves to the absolute opened repository path, including during linked-worktree execution.\\r\\n- Add `{{releases-folder}}`, resolving to the configured repository-relative releases path: `/`.\\r\\n- Support all three placeholders in action prompts, action commands, prompt preparation, diff commands, editor insertion controls, validation, and documentation.\\r\\n- Fail before process start when a required placeholder value is unavailable. Add tests for primary and linked-worktree execution, custom release paths, diff commands, insertion controls, and removed `{{rootProjectFolder}}` support.\\r\\n\\r\\n## acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Primary-checkout actions resolve `{{worktree-folder}}` and `{{project-folder}}` to the opened repository path.\\r\\n- Linked-worktree actions resolve `{{worktree-folder}}` to that worktree and `{{project-folder}}` to the opened repository path.\\r\\n- `{{releases-folder}}` returns the configured path relative to repository root, independent of active checkout.\\r\\n- Action prompts, action commands, and diff commands use the same three folder placeholders.\\r\\n- Editors and documentation list the new placeholders and no longer list `{{rootProjectFolder}}`.\\r\\n- `{{rootProjectFolder}}` is not resolved.\\r\\n\\n===== J_020_unify_agent_conversation_entries.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-020\\r\\ninternalId: 4edefccb-f7e3-4ae1-9c0d-5939ac1d3745\\r\\ntitle: unify agent conversation messages and events into ordered entries\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n - shared/agent_conversations.mjs\\r\\n - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_conversation.js\\r\\n - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js\\r\\n - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_transcript.js\\r\\n - app/src/data/data_types.ts\\r\\n - app/src/data/action_run_types.ts\\r\\n - app/src/services/actions/action_execution_service.ts\\r\\n - app/src/services/agents/card_agent_state.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/use_action_popup_controller.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_conversation_chat.tsx\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n checkLinting: true\\r\\n requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: c5d963f2-ca43-419d-bc3c-972199b7e7cd\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nReplace the parallel agent-conversation `messages` and `events` arrays with one canonical ordered `entries` array. Array position is ingestion order and is the only display order.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis refactor must land before the action-popup rendering-isolation work. That work must consume the single entry list and must not preserve the current merge-and-sort path.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Terminology\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Conversation entry**: one ordered item in an agent conversation.\\r\\n- **Message entry**: user or assistant text.\\r\\n- **Event entry**: reasoning, tool use, command execution, diagnostics, failures, and lifecycle observations.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not use **activity** for a conversation entry, field, helper, component, or collection. `activity` remains valid only for the separate card/project activity-storage domain.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current architecture\\r\\n\\r\\nPersisted `AgentConversation` stores `messages` and `events` separately. Live execution repeats the split as `LiveAgentTurn.messages` and `LiveAgentTurn.activities`. Producers append or replace items in those separate collections, while chat and transcript consumers merge and sort them by `sequence` to reconstruct ingestion order.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe split causes:\\r\\n\\r\\n- duplicate persisted and live representations;\\r\\n- inconsistent `event`/`activity` terminology;\\r\\n- repeated merge and sort work in consumers;\\r\\n- a rebuilt full `AgentConversation` projection in the popup controller;\\r\\n- ordering behavior owned by presentation code instead of the producer.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required model\\r\\n\\r\\nUse a discriminated union and one collection:\\r\\n\\r\\n```ts\\r\\n\\n===== J_021_derive_markdown_styles_globally.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-021\\r\\ninternalId: 11ffc4ac-44e0-4dab-a8d9-af9e83a43aff\\r\\ntitle: derive active Markdown content styles once in the global theme\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n - app/src/theme/theme_context.ts\\r\\n - app/src/theme/theme_provider.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/theme/theme_provider.test.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/theme/use_app_theme.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/editor/markdown_style_sx.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/editor/markdown_editor.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_conversation_chat.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/config/markdown_style_preview.tsx\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n checkLinting: true\\r\\n requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: 4edefccb-f7e3-4ae1-9c0d-5939ac1d3745\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nBuild the active Markdown content styling once when the global Markdown style configuration changes. Components that render active Markdown consume the stable derived style and never rebuild it during unrelated renders.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis job is independent of the action-popup subscription refactor and should land before performance verification of that refactor.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current architecture\\r\\n\\r\\n`AppThemeProvider` owns `markdownStyleConfig`, but consumers receive only the raw configuration. Both `MarkdownEditor` and `ActionConversationChat` call `buildMarkdownContentSx(markdownStyleConfig)` in their render bodies. The builder creates a new nested MUI style object even when the configuration is unchanged.\\r\\n\\r\\n`MarkdownStylePreview` also calls the builder, but it renders an explicit configuration draft rather than the active global style.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required change\\r\\n\\r\\n- Derive a stable `markdownContentSx` value in `AppThemeProvider` with `useMemo`, depending only on `markdownStyleConfig`.\\r\\n- Expose the derived value through `AppThemeContextValue` and its fallback value.\\r\\n- Make `MarkdownEditor` and `ActionConversationChat` consume `markdownContentSx` directly.\\r\\n- Do not call `buildMarkdownContentSx` from either component.\\r\\n- Keep `buildMarkdownContentSx` as a pure derivation function owned by the theme/style layer.\\r\\n- Memoize `MarkdownStylePreview`'s derived style by its explicit `config` prop. The preview cannot consume the active global style because it must show unsaved draft configuration.\\r\\n- Do not introduce a service class; this is a pure derived theme value.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Identity contract\\r\\n\\r\\n- `markdownContentSx` retains object identity across renders when `markdownStyleConfig` is unchanged.\\r\\n- Changing palette mode, popup state, editor content, conversation content, or unrelated configuration does not rebuild it.\\r\\n- Changing the active Markdown style configuration rebuilds it once and updates all active Markdown consumers.\\r\\n- Changing the preview's explicit draft configuration rebuilds only the preview value.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Testing implications\\r\\n\\r\\n- Theme-provider tests prove the derived style is exposed and retains identity across unrelated provider renders.\\r\\n- Theme-provider tests prove changing `markdownStyleConfig` replaces the derived value.\\r\\n\\n===== J_022_stabilize_action_prompt_drafts.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-022\\r\\ninternalId: 5b39ff1e-4bbc-4d50-b527-36e1d1faa6f5\\r\\ntitle: move action prompt drafts out of popup React state\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_prompt_draft.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_agent_prompt.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_popup_bottom_row.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_popup_content.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/use_action_popup_controller.ts\\r\\n - app/src/services/actions/action_execution_service.ts\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n checkLinting: true\\r\\n requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: 11ffc4ac-44e0-4dab-a8d9-af9e83a43aff\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nGive each action prompt draft one lifetime-stable external store. Typing, flushing, preparing, replacing, clearing, restoring, and remotely synchronizing a prompt must not place the prompt text or reset counters in `ActionPopupContent` or its controller React state.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis job must land before the major action-popup ownership and subscription refactor.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current architecture\\r\\n\\r\\nPrompt ownership is duplicated:\\r\\n\\r\\n- `useActionPopupController` stores prompt value, preparation status, and reset token in React state.\\r\\n- `ActionPopupContent` creates a new `ActionPromptDraft` whenever the controller prompt or reset token changes.\\r\\n- `ActionPromptDraft` buffers live editor values and supports a narrow bottom-row subscription.\\r\\n- `ActionExecutionService` separately stores prompt values, revisions, pending bridge writes, and remote prompt sessions.\\r\\n\\r\\nOrdinary typing already stays out of root React state because `MarkdownEditor.onLiveChange` writes to `ActionPromptDraft`. Editor flush still calls `setPromptState`, and external preparation/replacement/clear operations update root state and replace the draft object. Those paths rerender the complete popup.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required ownership\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate one prompt-draft service that owns stable draft stores keyed by the action context and, when applicable, the active agent session. The service is justified because it owns state, draft lifecycle, asynchronous bridge synchronization, revisions, and pending writes.\\r\\n\\r\\nMove the current prompt-draft map and remote prompt-session behavior out of `ActionExecutionService`. The renamed run/session service planned by the later popup refactor must not retain prompt text ownership.\\r\\n\\r\\nEach stable draft store exposes, at minimum:\\r\\n\\r\\n- current Markdown value;\\r\\n- preparation state: `loading`, `ready`, or `failed`;\\r\\n- a narrow subscription contract suitable for `useSyncExternalStore`;\\r\\n- local edit without React parent state;\\r\\n- external replacement that notifies the editor to call `setMarkdown` once;\\r\\n- clear, flush/synchronize, send, and current-value reads;\\r\\n- revision protection for superseded asynchronous preparation and remote writes.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not add arbitrary retention limits or silent eviction. Draft removal must follow explicit lifecycle events such as successful send, deliberate clear, action removal, or project teardown. A popup unmount does not discard an unsent draft.\\r\\n\\r\\n\\n===== J_023_use_one_agent_conversation_model.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-023\\r\\ninternalId: 1244ac27-293a-4a5f-b478-0890ecc3fea6\\r\\ntitle: use one agent conversation model while growing and persisted\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n - app/src/data/action_run_types.ts\\r\\n - app/src/data/data_types.ts\\r\\n - app/src/services/actions/action_execution_service.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/use_action_popup_controller.ts\\r\\n - desktop/src/actions/action/action_execution.js\\r\\n - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n checkLinting: true\\r\\n requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: 5b39ff1e-4bbc-4d50-b527-36e1d1faa6f5\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nFollow J-020 by removing the remaining `LiveAgentTurn` model. A growing conversation and a persisted conversation are the same `AgentConversation`; persistence is only a lifecycle state.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current problem\\r\\n\\r\\nJ-020 unified conversation content into `entries`, but renderer run state still stores `LiveAgentTurn`. `useActionPopupController` converts that object into a new `AgentConversation` during rendering. This duplicates models, metadata, and ownership.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required change\\r\\n\\r\\n- Remove `LiveAgentTurn` and `liveAgentConversation`.\\r\\n- Store `AgentConversation | null` directly in run state.\\r\\n- Make the agent-start event provide the complete canonical conversation snapshot, including identity, metadata, path, status, and initial entries.\\r\\n- Apply later message/event updates immutably to that conversation's `entries` without changing entry order.\\r\\n- Apply status and completion metadata to the same model.\\r\\n- Persist and reload the same `AgentConversation` shape.\\r\\n- Continuation starts from the canonical source conversation and adds new entries without a renderer-side merge.\\r\\n- Do not add live/persisted adapters, compatibility shapes, or duplicated fields.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] `LiveAgentTurn` and `liveAgentConversation` no longer exist.\\r\\n- [ ] Growing, completed, persisted, loaded, and continued conversations all use `AgentConversation`.\\r\\n- [ ] Run state exposes the canonical conversation directly.\\r\\n- [ ] Popup rendering performs no conversation-shape conversion or history merge.\\r\\n- [ ] Entry identity and order remain stable during streamed updates.\\r\\n- [ ] App and desktop lint and tests pass.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Dependency\\r\\n\\r\\nJ-020 must be implemented first.\\r\\n\\n===== J_024_replace_execution_state_with_scoped_action_runs.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-024\\r\\ninternalId: 1975a005-f0bb-432f-8ecb-bc85a27819d2\\r\\ntitle: replace global execution state with scoped action runs\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n - app/src/data/action_run_types.ts\\r\\n - app/src/data/electron_action_bridge.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/hooks/use_action_executions.ts\\r\\n - app/src/services/actions/action_execution_service.ts\\r\\n - Unrelated run changes must preserve selected store snapshots and must not render their consumers.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Persistence and lifecycle\\r\\n\\r\\n\\n===== J_025_move_action_popup_state_to_leaf_owners.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-025\\r\\ninternalId: 96705093-a302-409d-b626-fe3e16fd28e2\\r\\ntitle: move action popup state and subscriptions to leaf owners\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_popup.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_popup_content.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/use_action_popup_controller.ts\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_selector.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_conversation_chat.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_log_error_display.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_agent_approval.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_agent_question.tsx\\r\\n - app/src/components/actions/action_popup_bottom_row.tsx\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n checkLinting: true\\r\\n requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: 1975a005-f0bb-432f-8ecb-bc85a27819d2\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nMake popup roots own layout and selection only. Move changing application data, subscriptions, and operations to the smallest component that renders or acts on them.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required change\\r\\n\\r\\n- Remove `useActionPopupController`; do not replace it with another aggregate controller.\\r\\n- Remove active-run subscriptions from `ActionPopup` and `ActionPopupContent`.\\r\\n- Keep popup initialization as a one-time action/context binding lookup without subscribing the root.\\r\\n- Give `ActionSelector` a context-scoped status subscription.\\r\\n- Give the conversation section a subscription to only its bound run's canonical conversation.\\r\\n- Give status/log, approval, question, and run-control leaves their required run-store subscriptions.\\r\\n- Use the stable prompt store from J-022 only in the editor and prompt-dependent controls.\\r\\n- Put conversation-history loading and selection in the conversation owner, not the popup root.\\r\\n- Move schedule state and run-history loading to their existing leaf sections.\\r\\n- Event handlers read current service/store state when invoked; changing state is not routed through root props.\\r\\n- Do not use memoization as the ownership fix. Failed and declined reasoning already use the error presentation.\\n\\n## implementation details\\n\\n- Filter conversation feed activities in `ActionConversationChat`: omit only events where `type === 'reasoning'` and `status === 'completed'`.\\n- Keep in-progress, failed, declined and unknown-status reasoning visible.\\n- Keep completed reasoning events in conversation data and persisted history; this is a presentation-only change.\\n- Update chat tests for live completion, reopened conversations, failed/declined reasoning and unaffected non-reasoning activities.\\n\\n## acceptance criteria\\n\\n- In-progress reasoning is visible.\\n- A reasoning block disappears when its status becomes `completed`, including after reopening a conversation.\\n- Failed and declined reasoning remains visible with its error state and content.\\n- Completed non-reasoning activities remain visible.\\n\\r\\n\\n===== design\\\\releases\\\\0_0_4\\\\F_94_no_prefill_prompt_running_conv.md =====\\r\\n---\\nauthor: \\nid: F_94\\ninternalId: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\\ntitle: no prefill prompt running conv\\nstatus: ready\\nowner: \\naffects:\\nagents:\\npolicy:\\nafter: 3ffa4da3-1e0f-4930-ad38-6bf247b13c52\\n---\\n\\nWhen an agent is waiting for a response, but the action popup was closed or on the wrong 'action', then when the user clicks on the action to view the conversation and answer, the input box is prefilled again with the action's prompt. this is annoying cause it needs to be removed.\\n\\nso, when activating an action that has a running conversation, don't prefill the input\\n\\n# Current state\\n\\n`useActionPopupController` prepares an action's stored prompt for a new conversation. When popup opens on another action, or reopens while execution state is being restored, that prepared prompt can remain in `promptState` when user selects action with a `queued`, `running`, or `waitingForInput` conversation.\\n\\n# Implementation details\\n\\n- Give active execution its own prompt identity, including before active-child metadata arrives.\\n- When active action is selected, seed editor only from its shared user-entered draft; otherwise show empty input.\\n- Invalidate pending prompt preparation and bump `promptResetToken` when action becomes active.\\n- Keep stored-prompt prefill for idle actions starting new conversations. Keep command actions unchanged.\\n\\n# Acceptance criteria\\n\\n- Selecting or reopening action with active conversation does not prefill its stored action prompt.\\n- Existing user-entered draft for active conversation is restored.\\n- Late prompt-preparation result cannot overwrite active conversation input.\\n- Idle agent actions still prefill stored prompt.\\n- Controller and popup tests cover action switching, popup reopen, draft restore, and preparation race.\\n\\r\\n\\n===== design\\\\releases\\\\0_0_4\\\\F_95_integrate_into_project_should_track_commit.md =====\\r\\n---\\nauthor: \\nid: F_95\\ninternalId: e5b95f2c-cd0c-4623-8e12-d0c497447e71\\ntitle: integrate into project should track commit\\nstatus: ready\\nowner: \\naffects:\\nagents:\\n - design/activity/card__e5b95f2c-cd0c-4623-8e12-d0c497447e71.json#conversation=agent-4e6f97b9-647e-49fc-93f7-cf09e5eff1aa\\npolicy:\\nafter: 9ef42f8e-d6f7-4514-8e4a-5555318c4b51\\n---\\n\\n## Current state\\n\\n`WorktreeSelector` integrates an assigned card through `WorktreeService` and the Electron worktree service. The backend checkpoints primary-worktree changes, rebases the card branch when behind, then fast-forwards the project branch. The operation returns no commit metadata.\\n\\nCard commit history reads tracked `/activity/card__.json` files. Only action executions add commit references, so commits integrated from the selector are absent unless an action already recorded them.\\n\\n## Implementation details\\n\\n- Add a card-specific integration request containing `cardInternalId` and `projectFolder`; project-level worktree integration remains untracked.\\n- After any rebase, squash the card branch's complete change onto the project branch and create one integration commit. Do not fast-forward or retain the card branch's individual commits on the project branch.\\n- Resolve the integration commit's activity metadata, then append one system activity record containing only that commit and labeled `Integrate into project` to the card's primary-checkout activity file. Do not model it as a user action.\\n- Commit the activity-file update through the existing serialized activity writer. Return only after both integration and history persistence finish, so existing card-history reload and diff UI show the integration commit.\\n- If applying or committing the squash fails, restore the primary checkout to its state after the primary-worktree checkpoint and before the squash attempt.\\n- Failed integration writes no activity record. If integration succeeds but activity persistence fails, report that partial failure clearly; never claim tracking succeeded.\\n\\n## Acceptance criteria\\n\\n- Integrating a card worktree with one or several outgoing commits creates and records exactly one squash commit under the card's stable `internalId`.\\n- The squash commit contains the combined change between the project branch and the rebased card branch. Primary checkpoint and activity-file commits are not included.\\n- The squash commit appears once under `Integrate into project` in the existing card commit selector and opens one combined diff for the integration.\\n- Integration with no outgoing commits or no combined change remains rejected and creates no activity record.\\n- Failed integration creates no activity record. History-persistence failure after a successful squash commit is visible.\\n- Project-level worktree integration creates no card activity.\\n- Tests cover one and several source commits producing one squash commit, rebase before integration, stable card ownership, squash cleanup and persistence failure paths, and project-level exclusion.\\n\\r\\n\\n===== design\\\\releases\\\\0_0_4\\\\F_96_ctrl_enter_on_action_input.md =====\\r\\n---\\nauthor: \\nid: F_96\\ninternalId: d33002d3-ee0e-4c08-8e26-36f790500ee2\\ntitle: ctrl enter on action input\\nstatus: ready\\nowner: \\naffects:\\nagents:\\npolicy:\\nafter: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\\n---\\n\\nwhen pressing ctrl + enter on action input, the input is sent, this is good, but before this happens, the input box still adds an enter, which should not be the case.\\n\\n# Current state\\n\\n`ActionAgentPrompt` handles `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` on the prompt wrapper during event bubbling. The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges. ## File naming | Decision | Rule | Rationale | | --- | --- | --- | | Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. | ## Services and state | Decision | Rule | Rationale | | --- | --- | --- | | Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. | | Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. | | Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. | | Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. | ## Card state | Decision | Rule | Rationale | | --- | --- | --- | | The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. | | Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. | | Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. | ## Events and React integration | Decision | Rule | Rationale | | --- | --- | --- | | Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. | | Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. | | Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. | | Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. | --- internalId: a073f9b2-b7e9-42c1-9449-a8fb10c6a04e --- The renderer widely uses paths as runtime identifiers. The boundary between them is hard, and it is decided by location, not by content: - Markdown files in the **root of the working folder** are always cards. They must have an `internalId`; one is generated and persisted when missing. - Markdown files in the **archived or releases folder** are former cards and already carry an `internalId`. The boundary between them is hard, and it is decided by location, not by content: - Markdown files in the **root of the working folder** are always cards. They must have an `internalId`; one is generated and persisted when missing. - Markdown files in the **archived or releases folder** are former cards and already carry an `internalId`. A file there *without* an `internalId` is a regular markdown file. - **Any other** markdown file in the project is a regular markdown file. It never receives an `internalId`, and loading a project must not rewrite it. Consequences: - `after:` chains only ever link cards, so every participant in a chain has an `internalId`. - Regular markdown files are identified by path alone, everywhere. - A regular markdown file becomes a card only through an explicit user action that moves it into the working folder root; the `internalId` is written at that moment. # App Style Guide â€” Kanban / MDÂ² (React + MUI) How to build **any new component** so it matches the app. This is written for **Material UI v5+** components. **The theme is the source of truth.** All color, radius, base typography, and spacing units live in the single `createTheme` (defined in `GUIDANCE.md` Â§1/Â§9). This guide does **not** define colors â€” it tells you **which theme value to use for which role**, and covers the things the theme can't encode: layout, spacing/margins, borders, elevation, and component conventions. **The one rule that matters:** never write a raw hex, px radius, or magic color into a component. Read it from the theme (`theme.palette.*`, `theme.shape`, `theme.typography`, `theme.spacing`). If a component has a hardcoded hex in its `sx`/styled, it's wrong â€” that's exactly where the look drifts and where dark mode breaks. --- ## 1. How to consume the theme - **Colors:** `sx={{ color: 'text.secondary', bgcolor: 'background.paper', borderColor: 'divider' }}` â€” MUI resolves dotted palette paths automatically in `sx`. In `styled`/JS use the callback form: `styled(Box)(({ theme }) => ({ color: theme.palette.text.secondary }))`. - **Spacing:** use the 8px unit via the spacing scale â€” `sx={{ p: 2, gap: 1, mt: 1.5 }}` (`2` = 16px, `1` = 8px). Don't write `padding: '16px'`. - **Radius:** `borderRadius: 1` (= `theme.shape.borderRadius` = 8) and multiples; for the fixed non-8 radii see Â§4. - **Typography:** prefer `Typography variant=...` and `theme.typography.*` over ad-hoc `fontSize`. - **Custom tokens:** roles the default MUI palette doesn't cover (column/track surfaces, the strong/hover border steps, `text-3/4`, section-header color, `primary-bg` tint, status colors) must exist in the theme under a namespace (e.g. `theme.palette.custom.*`) with light + dark values. Consume them the same way â€” `bgcolor: 'custom.column'`. **Never inline their hex.** If a needed token doesn't exist yet, add it to the theme, don't hardcode it in the component. --- ## 2. Role â†’ theme slot Pick the slot by the element's **role**, not by how it looks in one mode: | Role | Theme slot | |---|---| | App background; tinted footer/action bars | `background.default` | | Column & sidebar surface | `custom.column` | | Segmented-control / toolbar track, hover fill | `custom.track` | | Card, dialog, popup, input surface | `background.paper` | | Hairlines, resting borders | `divider` | | Input borders, vertical separators | `custom.borderStrong` | | Border on hover | `custom.borderHover` | | Titles, values, headings | `text.primary` | | Body copy, field labels | `text.secondary` | | Meta, captions, resting icons | `custom.text3` | | Muted / placeholder / disabled | `custom.text4` | | Uppercase section/column headers | `custom.colHead` | | The one CTA, selection, focus, links, icon-hover | `primary.main` | | Contained-button hover | `primary.dark` | | Selected/tinted bg, focus ring, ID-chip bg | `custom.primaryBg` | | Text/icon on a primary fill | `primary.contrastText` | | Active / saved / online dot | `success.main` | | Destructive action | `error.main` | | Status swatch dots & ID-chip tints (decorative only) | `custom.status.*` | Rules: **one** `primary` per surface (the CTA/selection accent) â€” everything else is `text-*`/`divider`. Status colors are **decoration only** (dots, chip tints), never interactive color. Dark-mode brightness/tinting is handled inside the theme's two palettes, so a correctly-sloted component needs zero per-mode code. --- ## 3. Layout - **Full-height app:** column flex â€” menu row / ribbon / content (`flex: 1; minHeight: 0`) / status bar. Fixed bands `flexShrink: 0`. - **Board:** horizontal-scroll flex row, `gap: 2` (16px), page padding `p: 2.5` (20px); columns `width: 296, flexShrink: 0`, internal column flex `gap: 1`. - **List view:** two-pane flex row filling the space between ribbon and status bar â€” sidebar `width: 280, flexShrink: 0`, editor pane `flex: 1, minWidth: 0` (the `minWidth: 0` is required so long content ellipsizes instead of blowing out the row). - **Panels (sidebar, editor card, dialogs):** column flex with stacked bands (header / [toolbar] / body / footer). The **body scrolls** (`overflow-y: auto; minHeight: 0`); header and footer are `flexShrink: 0` and never scroll away. - **Spacer pattern:** push trailing items with `` rather than `margin-left: auto` sprinkled around, so rows stay predictable. - Use flex `gap` for spacing between siblings â€” don't hand-space with per-child margins. --- ## 4. Spacing, margin & size conventions - **4/8px grid, via `theme.spacing`.** page padding `2.5`; between columns `2`; inside columns / between related controls `1`; dialog body gap `2â€“2.25`; field labelâ†’control gap `~0.9` (7px). - **Margins:** prefer padding on containers + flex `gap` over element margins. Where a floating panel needs breathing room (e.g. editor card, toolbar inside a panel), use container padding (`p: 2 / 2.5`), not margins on the children. - **Fixed heights (px):** menu row 44, ribbon 52, status bar 32, section header 40, tab row 40, standard button / control 34, dense icon button 26â€“28, input 42. - **Fixed widths (px):** column 296, sidebar 280, search 260, standard dialog 480, wide/editor dialog 760. - **Radius family (px):** buttons/icon-buttons 8 (small 6â€“7), inputs 9, cards 10, columns/panels 12, dialogs/popups 14, chips/pills 99, color swatches 3. `borderRadius: 1` covers the 8 case; use explicit `'9px'` etc. for the others. --- ## 5. Borders & elevation - **Rest = border, not shadow.** Resting surfaces: `border: '1px solid'`, `borderColor: 'divider'`. Inputs use `custom.borderStrong`. **Shadow only when floating or lifted** (hover, drag, dialogs/popovers). - **Separation between bands:** a single 1px `divider` hairline. Don't stack a heavy rule *and* an outline â€” one line, let background contrast do the rest. Vertical separators inside toolbars: a 20px-tall `custom.borderStrong` rule. - **Elevation ladder (only where floating):** card hover `0 4px 12px rgba(16,24,40,0.12)`; dragging MUI `elevation 8` + `rotate(2deg)`; contained button `0 1px 2px rgba(16,24,40,0.15)`; dialog/popup `0 24px 60px rgba(16,24,40,0.28)`; scrim `rgba(16,24,40,0.45)` + `backdropFilter: blur(2px)`. - Set `MuiPaper.elevation: 0` and `MuiButton.disableElevation` globally in the theme; add the shadows above explicitly where the ladder calls for it. - **On dark backgrounds shadows read as nothing** â€” the theme already handles this by making hover raise `borderColor` (`custom.borderHover`) instead of relying on shadow. --- ## 6. Typography usage Drive everything from theme variants / `theme.typography`; avoid ad-hoc `fontSize`. - Titles/values/headings â†’ `text.primary`; body & labels â†’ `text.secondary`; meta â†’ `custom.text3`. - **Field labels:** a plain `Typography` (12px/600, `text.secondary`) placed **above** the control â€” **never** MUI floating/outlined `TextField` labels (they clash with the app's flat-label style). - **Section/column headers:** `Typography variant="overline"` (uppercase, `letterSpacing ~0.7px`, `fontWeight 700`, `custom.colHead`). - **ID chips only** use monospace; everything else is the theme's default family. - `button.textTransform: 'none'` and `button.fontWeight: 600` are set in the theme â€” don't re-uppercase buttons. --- ## 7. Interaction states Consistent across all components; all colors from the theme: - **Ghost icon button** (`IconButton`): transparent â†’ hover `bgcolor: track` (or `background.paper` on a colored panel) + `color: primary.main`. Override MUI's default circular hover tint via `sx`. - **Outlined button:** `divider` border, `text.secondary` â†’ hover `borderColor/color: primary.main`. Destructive: hover `borderColor: error.main` + `bgcolor: custom.dangerBg`. - **Contained (primary) CTA:** `primary.main` + small shadow â†’ hover `primary.dark`. - **Input/field focus:** `borderColor: primary.main` + `boxShadow: 0 0 0 3px` in `custom.primaryBg` (the soft halo). Unfocused hover: `borderColor: custom.borderHover`. - **List/tree row:** hover `bgcolor: track`; selected `bgcolor: custom.primaryBg` + title `text.primary`. - **Row-level actions** (delete, â‹®): hidden at rest, shown on `:hover`/`:focus-within` via **opacity** (keep in DOM so width doesn't jump). - **Active tab/menu item:** 2px `primary.main` bottom border + `primary.main` text. - Every icon-only control gets a `Tooltip` (theme sets `arrow: true`) **and** an `aria-label`. --- ## 8. Component conventions (MUI primitives) - **Buttons:** `Button variant="contained"` = the single CTA per surface; `variant="outlined"` = secondary; `variant="text"` = tertiary. Icon-only â†’ `IconButton` in a `Tooltip`. 1\n---\n\n## Problem\n\nA card worktree can be integrated into the project, but the user cannot review the complete card worktree diff before doing so. The card popup can show diffs for historical commits recorded in card activity, but it does not include the current worktree changes that are waiting to be integrated.\n\n## Required behavior\n\nAdd **View diff** to the same worktree menu as **Integrate into project**.\n\nThe new action must have exactly the same availability as **Integrate into project**. It is available only when the card has a valid assigned worktree with outgoing changes. If integration is unavailable, viewing the worktree diff is also unavailable.\n\nSelecting **View diff** shows the net changes the assigned card worktree would bring into the project branch. The diff covers the complete worktree change set, not only the card Markdown file or one agent commit. Use the card's existing diff-viewing experience, including the card body diff and navigation to other changed files.\n\nThe card popup's existing diff selector must also contain this worktree diff:\n\n- Show it as the first entry, above the historical commit diffs.\n- Label it clearly as the current worktree changes; do not present it as a commit.\n- Selecting it opens the same worktree diff as **View diff** in the worktree menu.\n- Keep the existing historical commit ordering and behavior unchanged.\n- Remove the entry as soon as **Integrate into project** is no longer available, including after successful integration.\n\nThe worktree diff is current repository state. Do not persist it in card activity and do not create a synthetic commit or activity record for it.\n\n## Implementation constraints\n\nThe current diff contract is commit-based and runs the configured commit diff command. Add a separate read-only worktree-diff operation rather than putting placeholder commit data into `CardCommit` or `ActivityCommitReference`.\n\nResolve the worktree through `WorktreeService` from the card's assigned worktree. The backend remains responsible for Git access and returns normalized per-file diff data to the renderer. Reading the diff must not commit, stage, rebase, merge, or otherwise change either worktree.\n\nModel the card popup selection as either a current worktree diff or a historical commit diff. Both entry points must use the same worktree-diff loading and presentation path. Derive availability from the same worktree status condition used by **Integrate into project** so the two controls cannot disagree.\n\nErrors while loading the diff must be reported through `dialogService` and leave the card popup in a safe state. An invalid or removed worktree must not fall back to the primary project folder.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- A card with an integratable assigned worktree shows **View diff** beside the existing worktree actions.\n- **View diff** is enabled if and only if **Integrate into project** is enabled.\n- The displayed diff is the complete net worktree change set that integration would apply to the project branch.\n- Added, modified, deleted, and renamed files that belong to that change set are represented correctly.\n- The card popup diff selector shows **Current worktree changes** as its first entry while integration is possible.\n- Selecting the menu action or the card popup entry opens the same diff.\n- Historical commit diffs remain below the new entry and retain their existing order and behavior.\n- The current worktree entry disappears after successful integration or whenever the worktree is no longer integratable.\n- Viewing the diff does not mutate Git state or write card activity.\n- Missing worktrees and Git failures are reported without showing a diff from another repository folder.\n\n## Tests\n\nAdd coverage for:\n\n1. Worktree diff generation across the project branch and assigned worktree.\n2. Added, modified, deleted, and renamed files in the returned diff.\n3. No Git mutation while reading a worktree diff.\n4. Matching availability of **View diff** and **Integrate into project**.\n5. The current worktree entry appearing first in the card popup diff selector.\n6. Both entry points selecting the same worktree diff.\n7. Removal of the entry after integration or loss of worktree eligibility.\n8. Existing historical commit selection and ordering remaining unchanged.\n9. "---\ninternalId: f2ec9e28-8064-4707-bce9-b62f24d57524\n---\n\n# App Style Guide â€” Kanban / MDÂ² (React + MUI)\n\nHow to build **any new component** so it matches the app. This is written for **Material UI v5+** components.\n\n**The theme is the source of truth.** All color, radius, base typography, and spacing units live in the single `createTheme` (defined in `GUIDANCE.md` Â§1/Â§9). This guide does **not** define colors â€” it tells you **which theme value to use for which role**, and covers the things the theme can't encode: layout, spacing/margins, borders, elevation, and component conventions.\n\n**The one rule that matters:** never write a raw hex, px radius, or magic color into a component. Read it from the theme (`theme.palette.*`, `theme.shape`, `theme.typography`, `theme.spacing`). If a component has a hardcoded hex in its `sx`/styled, it's wrong â€” that's exactly where the look drifts and where dark mode breaks.\n\n---\n\n## 1. How to consume the theme\n\n- **Colors:** `sx={{ color: 'text.secondary', bgcolor: 'background.paper', borderColor: 'divider' }}` â€” MUI resolves dotted palette paths automatically in `sx`. In `styled`/JS use the callback form: `styled(Box)(({ theme }) => ({ color: theme.palette.text.secondary }))`.\n- **Spacing:** use the 8px unit via the spacing scale â€” `sx={{ p: 2, gap: 1, mt: 1.5 }}` (`2` = 16px, `1` = 8px). Don't write `padding: '16px'`.\n- **Radius:** `borderRadius: 1` (= `theme.shape.borderRadius` = 8) and multiples; for the fixed non-8 radii see Â§4.\n- **Typography:** prefer `Typography variant=...` and `theme.typography.*` over ad-hoc `fontSize`.\n- **Custom tokens:** roles the default MUI palette doesn't cover (column/track surfaces, the strong/hover border steps, `text-3/4`, section-header color, `primary-bg` tint, status colors) must exist in the theme under a namespace (e.g. `theme.palette.custom.*`) with light + dark values. Consume them the same way â€” `bgcolor: 'custom.column'`. **Never inline their hex.** If a needed token doesn't exist yet, add it to the theme, don't hardcode it in the component.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Role â†’ theme slot\n\nPick the slot by the element's **role**, not by how it looks in one mode:\n\n| Role | Theme slot |\n|---|---|\n| App background; tinted footer/action bars | `background.default` |\n| Column & sidebar surface | `custom.column` |\n| Segmented-control / toolbar track, hover fill | `custom.track` |\n| Card, dialog, popup, input surface | `background.paper` |\n| Hairlines, resting borders | `divider` |\n| Input borders, vertical separators | `custom.borderStrong` |\n| Border on hover | `custom.borderHover` |\n| Titles, values, headings | `text.primary` |\n| Body copy, field labels | `text.secondary` |\n| Meta, captions, resting icons | `custom.text3` |\n| Muted / placeholder / disabled | `custom.text4` |\n| Uppercase section/column headers | `custom.colHead` |\n| The one CTA, selection, focus, links, icon-hover | `primary.main` |\n| Contained-button hover | `primary.dark` |\n| Selected/tinted bg, focus ring, ID-chip bg | `custom.primaryBg` |\n| Text/icon on a primary fill | `primary.contrastText` |\n| Active / saved / online dot | `success.main` |\n| Destructive action | `error.main` |\n| Status swatch dots & ID-chip tints (decorative only) | `custom.status.*` |\n\nRules: **one** `primary` per surface (the CTA/selection accent) â€” everything else is `text-*`/`divider`. Status colors are **decoration only** (dots, chip tints), never interactive color. Dark-mode brightness/tinting is handled inside the theme's two palettes, so a correctly-sloted component needs zero per-mode code.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Layout\n\n- **Full-height app:** column flex â€” menu row / ribbon / content (`flex: 1; minHeight: 0`) / status bar. Fixed bands `flexShrink: 0`.\n- **Board:** horizontal-scroll flex row, `gap: 2` (16px), page padding `p: 2.5` (20px); columns `width: 296, flexShrink: 0`, internal column flex `gap: 1`.\n- **List view:** two-pane flex row filling the space between ribbon and status bar â€” sidebar `width: 280, flexShrink: 0`, editor pane `flex: 1, minWidth: 0` (the `minWidth: 0` is required so long content ellipsizes instead of blowing out the row).\n- **Panels (sidebar, editor card, dialogs):** column flex with stacked bands (header / [toolbar] / body / footer). The **body scrolls** (`overflow-y: auto; minHeight: 0`); header and footer are `flexShrink: 0` and never scroll away.\n- **Spacer pattern:** push trailing items with `` rather than `margin-left: auto` sprinkled around, so rows stay predictable.\n- Use flex `gap` for spacing between siblings â€” don't hand-space with per-child margins.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Spacing, margin & size conventions\n\n- **4/8px grid, via `theme.spacing`.** page padding `2.5`; between columns `2`; inside columns / between related controls `1`; dialog body gap `2â€“2.25`; field labelâ†’control gap `~0.9` (7px).\n- **Margins:** prefer padding on containers + flex `gap` over element margins. Where a floating panel needs breathing room (e.g. editor card, toolbar inside a panel), use container padding (`p: 2 / 2.5`), not margins on the children.\n- **Fixed heights (px):** menu row 44, ribbon 52, status bar 32, section header 40, tab row 40, standard button / control 34, dense icon button 26â€“28, input 42.\n- **Fixed widths (px):** column 296, sidebar 280, search 260, standard dialog 480, wide/editor dialog 760.\n- **Radius family (px):** buttons/icon-buttons 8 (small 6â€“7), inputs 9, cards 10, columns/panels 12, dialogs/popups 14, chips/pills 99, color swatches 3. `borderRadius: 1` covers the 8 case; use explicit `'9px'` etc. for the others.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Borders & elevation\n\n- **Rest = border, not shadow.** Resting surfaces: `border: '1px solid'`, `borderColor: 'divider'`. Inputs use `custom.borderStrong`. **Shadow only when floating or lifted** (hover, drag, dialogs/popovers).\n- **Separation between bands:** a single 1px `divider` hairline. Don't stack a heavy rule *and* an outline â€” one line, let background contrast do the rest. Vertical separators inside toolbars: a 20px-tall `custom.borderStrong` rule.\n- **Elevation ladder (only where floating):** card hover `0 4px 12px rgba(16,24,40,0.12)`; dragging MUI `elevation 8` + `rotate(2deg)`; contained button `0 1px 2px rgba(16,24,40,0.15)`; dialog/popup `0 24px 60px rgba(16,24,40,0.28)`; scrim `rgba(16,24,40,0.45)` + `backdropFilter: blur(2px)`.\n- Set `MuiPaper.elevation: 0` and `MuiButton.disableElevation` globally in the theme; add the shadows above explicitly where the ladder calls for it.\n- **On dark backgrounds shadows read as nothing** â€” the theme already handles this by making hover raise `borderColor` (`custom.borderHover`) instead of relying on shadow.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Typography usage\n\nDrive everything from theme variants / `theme.typography`; avoid ad-hoc `fontSize`.\n\n- Titles/values/headings â†’ `text.primary`; body & labels â†’ `text.secondary`; meta â†’ `custom.text3`.\n- **Field labels:** a plain `Typography` (12px/600, `text.secondary`) placed **above** the control â€” **never** MUI floating/outlined `TextField` labels (they clash with the app's flat-label style).\n- **Section/column headers:** `Typography variant=\"overline\"` (uppercase, `letterSpacing ~0.7px`, `fontWeight 700`, `custom.colHead`).\n- **ID chips only** use monospace; everything else is the theme's default family.\n- `button.textTransform: 'none'` and `button.fontWeight: 600` are set in the theme â€” don't re-uppercase buttons.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Interaction states\n\nConsistent across all components; all colors from the theme:\n\n- **Ghost icon button** (`IconButton`): transparent â†’ hover `bgcolor: track` (or `background.paper` on a colored panel) + `color: primary.main`. Override MUI's default circular hover tint via `sx`.\n- **Outlined button:** `divider` border, `text.secondary` â†’ hover `borderColor/color: primary.main`. Destructive: hover `borderColor: error.main` + `bgcolor: custom.dangerBg`.\n- **Contained (primary) CTA:** `primary.main` + small shadow â†’ hover `primary.dark`.\n- **Input/field focus:** `borderColor: primary.main` + `boxShadow: 0 0 0 3px` in `custom.primaryBg` (the soft halo). Unfocused hover: `borderColor: custom.borderHover`.\n- **List/tree row:** hover `bgcolor: track`; selected `bgcolor: custom.primaryBg` + title `text.primary`.\n- **Row-level actions** (delete, â‹®): hidden at rest, shown on `:hover`/`:focus-within` via **opacity** (keep in DOM so width doesn't jump).\n- **Active tab/menu item:** 2px `primary.main` bottom border + `primary.main` text.\n- Every icon-only control gets a `Tooltip` (theme sets `arrow: true`) **and** an `aria-label`.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Component conventions (MUI primitives)\n\n- **Buttons:** `Button variant=\"contained\"` = the single CTA per surface; `variant=\"outlined\"` = secondary; `variant=\"text\"` = tertiary. Icon-only â†’ `IconButton` in a `Tooltip`. Don't use `Link` or text `Button` where an action button belongs (that reproduces the old text-link look).\n- **Icons:** `@mui/icons-material` **Outlined** variants; `fontSize: 18` in 34px buttons, `16` in dense, `13â€“15` inline. Don't hand-draw SVG.\n- **ID chip:** monospace, accent text on `custom.primaryBg`/status tint, `radius 5, flexShrink: 0`.\n- **Count chip:** `background.paper` bg, 1px `divider`, radius 9â€“10, `custom.text3`.\n- **State dot:** 7â€“8px circle + `text-3` label; green (`success.main`) = active/saved/online.\n- **Search:** pill `TextField` (`borderRadius: 99`, `bgcolor: background.default`), search start-adornment, `âŒ˜K` keycap end-adornment.\n- **Select:** `size=\"small\"`, optional dot+name via `renderValue`; 42px / radius-9 frame. When a select has a tooltip, keep the tooltip available while the select is closed and explicitly hide it for the entire time the select menu is open so it cannot cover the first option.\n- **Segmented control** (view switch, formatting toolbar): `ToggleButtonGroup` on a `custom.track` background; selected segment `background.paper` + `0 1px 2px` shadow + `primary` text.\n- **Dialog / popup:** `Dialog`/`Popover` with `PaperProps` â†’ `background.paper`, 1px `divider`, radius 14, big shadow; scrim via `slotProps.backdrop` (blur + tint). Bands separated by hairlines; footer on a `background.default` bar with top hairline; actions right-aligned (outlined Cancel + contained CTA). `autoFocus` first field; submit on `Enter` (`âŒ˜/Ctrl+Enter` in a textarea); close on `Esc`/backdrop.\n- **Empty state:** dashed target â€” `1.5px dashed custom.borderStrong`, radius 10, centered icon + `custom.text4` label. No \"click to add\" placeholder blocks.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Definition of done for a new component\n\n1. Zero hardcoded hex / raw px colors â€” every value comes from `theme.palette` / `theme.shape` / `theme.spacing` / `theme.typography`.\n2. Correct roleâ†’slot mapping (Â§2); at most one `primary` CTA on the surface.\n3. Borders at rest, shadow only when floating (Â§5); bands split by a single hairline.\n4. Hover **and** focus states on every interactive element (Â§7); icon buttons have tooltip + `aria-label`.\n5. Body scrolls, header/footer pinned; `minWidth: 0` on flex children that hold long text.\n6. Toggle to dark mode and confirm nothing breaks â€” if it does, you hardcoded a color somewhere (Â§1).\n\nComponent-specific detail lives in `GUIDANCE.md` (theme definition + board/list/dialog), `CARD_POPUP_GUIDE.md`, `RUN_DIALOG_GUIDE.md`, and `SIDEBAR_ACTIONS_GUIDE.md`.\n\r\n", design\releases\0_1_0\card__290f3413-3d14-4ec2-b97d-e2522c3c1057.json:1187: "output": "---\ninternalId: f2ec9e28-8064-4707-bce9-b62f24d57524\n---\n\n# App Style Guide â€” Kanban / MDÂ² (React + MUI)\n\nHow to build **any new component** so it matches the app. This is written for **Material UI v5+** components.\n\n**The theme is the source of truth.** All color, radius, base typography, and spacing units live in the single `createTheme` (defined in `GUIDANCE.md` Â§1/Â§9). 'integrate into project' again, the app gives an error to say nothing left to integrate. then the icon gets updated correctly\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`WorktreeSelector` derives its arrows and enabled actions from records published by `WorktreeService`. Integration creates a squash commit on the project branch, but leaves the linked branch on its original commits. Git therefore still reports the worktree as ahead and behind. A second integration rebases away those already-integrated commits, publishes the corrected state, then fails because nothing remains to integrate.\\r\\n\\r\\nCard integration also commits its activity record after the integration refresh, so that new project commit is absent from the published status.\\r\\n\\r\\n## implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- After a successful squash, move the clean linked branch to the integration commit before publishing worktree state. Keep its assignment and branch; do not park or unassign it.\\r\\n- After card activity persistence completes, synchronize the linked branch to the new project head and publish worktree state again.\\r\\n- Keep project-level integration on the shared synchronization path; it needs no activity refresh.\\r\\n- Preserve existing integration and activity-persistence errors. Existing renderer subscription should update without component-local state.\\r\\n\\r\\n## acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Successful integration immediately removes the outgoing indicator and disables `Integrate into project`.\\r\\n- Card integration finishes with no outgoing or incoming indicator and disables both integration and update actions.\\r\\n- Reopening the selector or waiting for polling is unnecessary.\\r\\n- A second integration is not required to correct the icon and is unavailable when no outgoing changes remain.\\r\\n- Card and project integrations publish correct final worktree status; failure behavior remains unchanged.\\r\\n\\n===== B_81_new_card_markdown_typing_lag.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: B_81\\r\\ninternalId: 8e4a295a-8788-4232-8be7-c97f5a1cf5c8\\r\\ntitle: new card Markdown typing lag\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: ff356504-eed4-47f3-bb38-2c749b6fcba6\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Problem\\r\\n\\r\\nTyping in the **New card** description editor has noticeable input lag.\\r\\n\\r\\nPerformance trace `Trace-20260731T140458.json` records five input events that each block the renderer main thread for 52-64 ms. Layout and paint are small; synchronous React work consumes most of the time.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Cause\\r\\n\\r\\n`NewCardDialog` passes `handleBodyChange` to `MarkdownEditor.onLiveChange`. Every editor change calls `setBody`, rerendering the complete dialog and the MDXEditor subtree. This also recreates the Markdown editor plugin array and many MUI elements and style objects. Development-mode React work and garbage collection amplify the cost.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis bypasses the lifetime-stable editor approach already used by `CardEditor` and `CardBodyEditor`. `MarkdownEditor` already buffers local edits and exposes `getMarkdown`, `setMarkdown`, and `flush`; normal typing does not need to propagate the full body into parent React state.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required change\\r\\n\\r\\n- Keep the new-card Markdown editor lifetime-stable while typing, following `CardEditor` and `CardBodyEditor`.\\r\\n- Do not store the full Markdown body in `NewCardDialog` state on every keystroke.\\r\\n- Read the current body from the editor when submitting, checking whether the draft is dirty, and inserting or clearing the template.\\r\\n- Preserve existing template behavior: untouched template can be cleared; editing it changes the action back to `Template`; inserting then appends without discarding text.\\r\\n- Keep reset, cancel confirmation, `Ctrl+Enter`, and target-column behavior unchanged.\\r\\n- Do not change shared `MarkdownEditor` buffering semantics solely for this dialog.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] Typing in the new-card description does not rerender `NewCardDialog` or remount/rerender the Markdown editor for every keystroke.\\r\\n- [ ] Submitted card body exactly matches current editor content.\\r\\n- [ ] Cancel confirmation detects description-only edits.\\r\\n- [ ] Template insert, clear, edit, and append behavior remains unchanged.\\r\\n- [ ] Opening, closing, successful creation, and project changes reset the draft correctly.\\r\\n- [ ] A regression test verifies repeated description edits do not repeatedly render the editor boundary.\\r\\n- [ ] Existing new-card dialog and Markdown editor tests pass.\\r\\n\\n===== B_82_orphaned_git_for_windows_processes.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: B_82\\r\\ninternalId: d97a054f-5a67-47bb-9070-df874cf9148e\\r\\ntitle: agent runs leave orphaned Git for Windows processes\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 7bdf27fc-963c-4545-83e2-93410e67f0e3\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Problem\\r\\n\\r\\nAgent runs launched through MDÂ² can leave multiple `git.exe` processes running indefinitely. The processes appear as **Git for Windows** in Task Manager and accumulate across runs.\\r\\n\\r\\nObserved processes were executing normally short-lived commands such as `config`, `rev-parse`, `remote -v`, and `status --porcelain`. They remained alive after their immediate parent processes had exited.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current implementation\\r\\n\\r\\nMDÂ² starts agents through `AgentRunnerService`. When an agent closes normally, `handleClose` queries the current Windows process tree and terminates descendants of the agent PID. Cancellation terminates the process tree with `taskkill /t /f`.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis cleanup cannot discover a surviving Git process after an intermediate parent has already exited: the current process snapshot no longer contains a complete chain from the agent PID to that Git process. The observed Git processes had dead immediate parents, matching this failure mode.\\r\\n\\r\\nMDÂ² also invokes Git directly through `git_commands.js`. These calls have no timeout or cancellation handling, so an independently hung app-owned Git command can block its caller indefinitely.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Investigation plan\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Reproduce with MDÂ² open but no agent run, then while starting and completing or cancelling an agent run.\\r\\n2. Record every spawned Git PID, command, working directory, parent PID, agent run ID, and lifecycle event.\\r\\n3. Run an affected command under a bounded external timeout with Git tracing enabled to locate the blocking operation.\\r\\n4. Check repository state, Git configuration, filesystem monitoring, antivirus or file locks, and agent shutdown ordering.\\r\\n5. Confirm whether Git descendants become disconnected before `AgentRunnerService.handleClose` takes its process snapshot.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required change\\r\\n\\r\\n- Track enough process ownership during an agent run to terminate surviving descendants even when intermediate processes exit before final cleanup.\\r\\n- Clean up owned descendants when an agent completes, fails, is cancelled, or crashes.\\r\\n- Do not terminate unrelated Git processes or Git work started outside the corresponding MDÂ² agent run.\\r\\n- Add a bounded timeout and process cleanup to direct Git execution in `git_commands.js`.\\r\\n- Include the command, working directory, elapsed time, and owning run or app operation in timeout diagnostics.\\r\\n- Deduplicate or serialize repeated read-only metadata probes only if tracing confirms they contribute to the accumulation.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Failure modes and compatibility\\r\\n\\r\\n- PID reuse must not allow cleanup to target a process that MDÂ² did not start.\\r\\n- Cleanup must cover shell and helper-process chains used by Git for Windows on Windows.\\r\\n- Long-running network Git operations need an explicit, suitable timeout rather than the same threshold as local metadata commands.\\r\\n- Existing agent cancellation, command actions, commits, worktree operations, push, pull, and fetch behavior must remain unchanged apart from bounded failure and cleanup.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] Completing, failing, cancelling, or crashing an agent run leaves no Git processes owned by that run.\\r\\n- [ ] Repeated agent runs do not accumulate Git for Windows processes.\\r\\n\\n===== B_85_add_the_reference_to_a_chatlog_to_a_card_as_soon_as_possible.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: B_85\\r\\ninternalId: 56dd54b0-9554-4545-85d4-bb45efef4d6e\\r\\ntitle: add the reference to a chatlog to a card as soon as possible\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\n - After history is selected, `handleConversationChange` only loads persisted paths, so popup cannot return to empty conversation state.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Keep empty `Conversations` item selectable while picker is enabled.\\r\\n- Treat empty value as reset: clear selected conversation and displayed chat without calling conversation loader.\\r\\n- Next run omits `continueFrom` and starts new conversation.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- User can select `Conversations` after selecting historical conversation.\\r\\n- Popup returns to empty conversation without error or empty-path load.\\r\\n- Next run starts new conversation; selecting history still continues selected conversation.\\r\\n- Picker and controller tests cover reset and continuation behavior.\\r\\n\\n===== F_115_add_support_for_request_approval.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_115\\r\\ninternalId: 7bdf27fc-963c-4545-83e2-93410e67f0e3\\r\\ntitle: add support for request approval\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 56dd54b0-9554-4545-85d4-bb45efef4d6e\\r\\n---\\r\\n# Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`CodexStreamingAdapter` handles structured questions, but not Codex app-server approval requests. `item/fileChange/requestApproval` and `item/commandExecution/requestApproval` fall through as protocol diagnostics, for example `item/fileChange/requestApproval: unknown (...)`. Show policy-amendment choices only when Codex supplies them.\\r\\n- Support multiple pending approvals without overwriting one another. Existing completed command/file activity remains authoritative.\\r\\n- Add adapter, runner, execution-contract, bridge, remote-control, service, popup, reload, and regression tests. Run lint and tests in `desktop/` and `app/`.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- File-change and command-execution approval requests show actionable prompts instead of protocol diagnostics.\\r\\n- Allow once/session, decline, stop-turn, and offered policy-amendment choices send the exact matching JSON-RPC decision and unblock Codex.\\r\\n- Approval UI shows available security context before user decides, including network-specific context when present.\\r\\n- Concurrent requests remain isolated; `serverRequest/resolved`, turn completion, or cancellation removes only matching pending requests.\\r\\n- Renderer reload and remote-control clients retain correct pending approval state.\\r\\n- Structured questions, activity ordering, changed-path tracking, and conversation persistence keep existing behavior; approval data is not persisted.\\r\\n\\n===== F_89_add_support_for_clicking_on_links_in_chatlogs.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_89\\r\\ninternalId: 9ef42f8e-d6f7-4514-8e4a-5555318c4b51\\r\\ntitle: add support for clicking on links in chatlogs\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: e69b9faf-30dd-4ad6-9d99-7e6af4d18c76\\r\\n---\\r\\nSometimes the agent produces a link to a local project file.
